title: Supervised visual-polish batch (full-width layout, header/eyebrow cleanup, timeline flatten, detail reorder, analysis de-badge) - applied in-session, needs commit + tests

title: Mobile UX + visual language: mobile shell (bottom-nav + Detail bottom-sheet) and a color/shade classification system
context: Mobile UX + visual-language workstream, from an operator UX review (post-FU-1). Two intertwined problems. (1) Mobile interaction model: the mobile view stacks the desktop four columns into one long scroll, so browse -> inspect -> place -> review becomes scroll-heavy and forces manual closing to reach the next action. UX principles from the operator: sequential actions should be visually grouped; minimize scrolling; never require manually closing something to get to the next action. Proposed direction: a mobile shell with a bottom nav / segmented control of about 3 views (Build = Library, Pot = Timeline, Read = Balance/Cuisine/Advisories), header actions (How/Recipe/Save/Load) moved to a top app-bar or menu; and Detail becomes a bottom sheet that opens on card tap, shows metadata plus the Place-in-stage chips, and auto-dismisses on placement so the user returns to browsing with no manual close. (2) Visual language: the theme is near-monochrome dark with a single orange accent, so navigation and content read as one plane. Introduce color and shade in three roles: classification hues for the 11 categories and 8 cooking stages (a stage color reused consistently across its place-in-stage chip, its timeline lane, and any reference so color teaches the mapping); severity colors for advisories (info / warning / suggestion / timing); and elevation/shade so nav and section headers are visually distinct from content. Recommended approach: start with a static HTML mockup/spike (like design/ui-spike.html) to lock the mobile shell and color palette before rewiring components, then implement and iterate on-device. Open decisions: confirm the bottom-nav + bottom-sheet model vs alternatives (wizard/step flow, or single-scroll with sticky section jumps); mockup-first vs live prototype. Also fold in stale-mobile-CSS cleanup: the column presets switch at 768px but an old max-width:720px block still sets flex-direction:column on .ingredient-row, .stage-card__header, and .summary-header (now grids, largely inert), leaving a 721-767px dead zone - realign the breakpoints and purge the stale rules as part of this.
trigger: Operator UX review of the mobile version: not actively broken, but the stacked-columns model is scroll-heavy and requires manually closing panels to advance, and the near-monochrome dark theme lacks navigation and classification cues.
resolution: Superseded by D-37; scope moved into Phases 7-10 (mobile shell + visual language in Phase 9). Residual visual-language ideas (per-stage colors, advisory severity colors, elevation/shade) live in design v2.md and this FU's history if revived later.

title: Cook-method model + pressure/release input (relight timing-findings and recipe timing)
context: Pressure/release UI was removed during the timeline flatten (FU-1 era). The pressureMinutes and naturalReleaseMinutes fields remain on StewBuild and in persistence, and are actively consumed: analysis.ts timing-findings short-circuit when pressureMinutes is undefined then compare each ingredient cook window against it (the X-is-overcooked-at-N-min-pressure advisories), and instructions.ts uses both to state cook/release times in the generated recipe. With no input to set them, both timing-findings and recipe timing are currently DARK for user-created builds. onUpdateBuild is now dead wiring in BuildSummary/App. During the Phase-6 reconcile the operator deferred this as its own item because the design is broader than one input: pressure-cooking is Instant-Pot-specific, but the app could also target dutch oven, slow cooker, or stovetop, where pressure minutes does not apply. The real question is a cook-method model (method selector -> method-appropriate timing inputs -> method-aware timing-findings + recipe), not just re-adding a pressure box. Options: (a) re-add pressure/release input as-is to relight timing for pressure builds; (b) build a cook-method model; (c) drop pressure/release + timing-findings entirely. Operator needs to think more.
trigger: Phase-6 punch-list reconcile: pressure/release input was removed, leaving timing-findings analysis and recipe timing dark; operator wants a broader cook-method design before re-adding.

title: Phase-6 polish: Detail dismiss + focus-return a11y and pairing count-once test
context: Deferred from the Phase-6 punch-list reconcile as low-priority MVP polish. (a) Library-click-dismiss: clicking within the Library should dismiss the open Detail panel; currently only Escape and the Close button do. (b) Focus-return: after the Detail panel closes, and after a saved-build restore via the Load modal, keyboard focus should return to a sensible element rather than being lost. (c) Pairing count-once test: assert a pairing advisory fires exactly once when a build contains both a group and one of its members and the ingredient pairsWith both refs, guarding the makePairKey seen-set dedup (already works, covered indirectly). Keyboard and click alternatives already exist, so none of these block the MVP.
trigger: Phase-6 punch-list reconcile: small a11y (Detail dismiss / focus-return) and one dedup regression test, not worth blocking the MVP close.
